newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI'S LAID-OFF WORKERS ELIGIBLE FOR LOANS.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI'S LAID-OFF WORKERS ELIGIBLE FOR LOANS.

text.p: The Shanghai City Cooperative Bank, at the behest of the city government, will provide low-interest loans to people who have been laid off to help them start their own businesses, the Business News said on Thursday.
The loans would be sourced from local re-employment funds and administration funds for provincial labourers, the newspaper said.
The interest rate was temporarily fixed at 0.756 percent per month, it said but gave no further details.
China's basic loan interest rate is around eight to nine percent annually, rising according to the period and type of loan, official figures show.
People who have been laid off in China are not counted among the unemployed because their state firms keep them on the payroll and cover basic living costs.
Official figures show that Shanghai has 150,000 unemployed people, but that so-called laid-off workers number more than one million.
